model: Life insurer FCFE at cost of equity (core earnings to common x distributable conversion, engine route, net debt held at zero)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: core EPS growth FY2025 (8%), below the 10-12% medium-term target; aggregate core earnings growth in the base case runs 7.5-8% fading to 3.5%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (2.6%, FY2022 IFRS17-restated common ~40.2bn -> FY2025 43.5bn) diverges >30% from EPS/core EPS growth: buybacks of 1.6-3.3bn/yr and AOCI swings suppress common equity, and the CSM (post-tax ~22.7bn net of NCI) sits outside IFRS equity. Revenue is not meaningful for a life insurer (IFRS 4 revenue swung 17bn-80bn on investment marks); 3/5-yr CAGRs across the FY2022/23 IFRS 17 break are left null.
historical_growth.notes: Reported FCF/OCF is not a usable series for an insurer (FY2025 OCF 32.1bn vs core earnings 7.5bn) and SBC is not adjusted separately; the owner-flow series is FCFE = dividends + buybacks.

scenario_narratives.base: Manulife delivers the low-middle of its 10-12% core EPS target: aggregate core earnings to common grow ~7.5-8% through 2029 on Asia and Global WAM, with ~2.5% annual buyback shrink. About 72-80% of core earnings is distributed via a 35-45% dividend payout plus NCIB buybacks. Valued as a perpetual FCFE stream at a 9.5% CAD cost of equity, capped at 14x terminal FCFE (~11x core earnings).
scenario_narratives.bull: Asia reaches half of core earnings, core ROE clears the 18% 2027 target, the LTC reinsurance with Munich Re de-risks the U.S. book and frees capital, and Global WAM scales on record gross flows. Core earnings compound ~9-10% for five years and the market sustains a premium multiple at a 9% cost of equity.
scenario_narratives.bear: A China/Hong Kong regulatory or geopolitical shock slows Asia new business, Canada's claims experience stays weak and a reserve charge on the retained LTC block forces Manulife to throttle buybacks to defend LICAT. Core earnings grow only 3-4.5% and the stock trades at a mature-insurer multiple on a 10.5% cost of equity.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Manulife is valued on what it can distribute to common shareholders, not on accounting book: core earnings available to common (after preferred/LRCN distributions and holdco interest) times a distributable conversion, discounted at a CAD cost of equity with no debt deduction. IFRS 17 book (BVPS 27.48) excludes the 22.7bn net-of-NCI CSM, so the cross-check anchor is adjusted BVPS (41.12 at Jun-26): the base value should sit at a P/adjusted-book consistent with a 16-18% core ROE business earning above a ~9.5% cost of equity.
key_risks_to_valuation: China/Hong Kong regulatory or geopolitical shock to Asia (47% of core earnings, target 50%)
Retained U.S. long-term care reserve risk despite three reinsurance transactions
Core-to-net-income gap: core earnings exclude market experience and basis changes; persistent net-income shortfalls (FY2023-25 ~76% of core) mean core overstates distributable earnings if they recur
Interest-rate and equity-market sensitivity of Global WAM fees and CSM
Terminal value share is high in an FCFE model at a 9.5% cost of equity; the 14x FCFE cap is the binding discipline
valuation_philosophy.cross_check: Base IV 64.06 = 1.56x adjusted BVPS (41.12, Jun-26) and ~13.8x FY2026E core EPS (~4.65: H1 2.15 + H2 at ~+10% on 2025's 2.27). The market price sits at ~1.47x adjusted book and ~13x forward core EPS. All three scenarios are bound by the terminal FCFE cap (14x/16x/11x), not Gordon; terminal share of value 45-60%.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 44.16-63.58
data_sources.financials: MFC.TO_Metrics.csv (core_metrics); Q2-2026 Report to Shareholders and press release (core earnings to common, adjusted BVPS, share count, NCIB); FY2025 Annual MD&A (targets table, remittances); Q4-2025 press release (FY2025 core earnings to common, buybacks)

inputs.sbc_source: Not deducted separately: core earnings are after stock-based compensation expense (MFC expenses its equity-settled awards through core expenses; FY2025 FS note shows equity-contract hedges of the SBC liability). Share count held flat because buybacks are inside the FCFE stream.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T20:00:00Z regular close (TSX), Yahoo Finance chart API
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,659.2m common shares outstanding at 31 Jul 2026 (Q2-2026 MD&A, line 1773) plus ~4m option dilution (Q2-2026 diluted weighted average 1,670m vs 1,662m period-end) = 1,663m. Held FLAT: NCIB repurchases (FY2025 $2.43bn, H1-2026 $0.97bn) are part of the FCFE distributed and valued here; shrinking the count as well would double-count them.
inputs.base_revenue_note: 'Revenue' in this engine route is FY2025 core earnings available to common shareholders, CAD 7,200m (Q4-2025 press release line 849; Q2-2026 MD&A core-ROE reconciliation). Already after preferred/LRCN distributions (321m), after holdco interest and after tax, so capitalised at the cost of equity with no debt deduction.
inputs.ebitda_margin_note: The margin path is the FCFE conversion: share of core earnings available to common that is distributable (dividends + buybacks) after the capital retained to fund new-business CSM/LICAT. Actuals: FY2025 dividends ~2,992m (DPS 1.76 x ~1,700m avg shares) + buybacks 2,431m = 5,423m = 75% of core to common; FY2024 ~89% (boosted by a reinsurance capital release); remittances 6.4bn FY2025 / 7.0bn FY2024. The conversion also absorbs the persistent gap between core earnings and IFRS net income (FY2023-25 common net income averaged ~76% of core: market experience, LTC/VA basis changes).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in CAD, the flows' currency: Government of Canada 10y ~3.3% + beta ~1.15 x 5.25% ERP = ~9.3%, rounded to 9.5% base. Bull 9.0% (de-risked balance sheet after three LTC/VA reinsurance deals, LICAT 136%); bear 10.5% (Asia regulatory/China exposure, retained LTC tail). Flows are post-interest and post-preferred, so no WACC blend and no net-debt deduction.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable; lease cost sits inside core expenses.
inputs.nci_treatment: Core earnings and CSM figures used are net of NCI (attributed to shareholders); preferred shares and LRCNs (6,660m) excluded via the core-earnings-available-to-common basis.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Life insurer FCFE at cost of equity via the component engine (net debt = 0, D&A/capex/tax/SBC/WC all zero so FCFE = core earnings to common x conversion). The routing table's default for insurers is BVPS compounding x exit P/B; overridden to FCFE-at-CoE following the GL/PRU/MET life-insurer precedent in this folder, because IFRS 17 common equity (BVPS 27.48) excludes the post-tax CSM (adjusted BVPS 41.12 at Jun-26) and the IFRS 4 -> IFRS 17 restatement breaks the book series at FY2022, so book is not a usable compounding base. Cross-check: base IV / adjusted BVPS 41.12 and implied P/core earnings are recorded in valuation_philosophy. FY0 = FY2025 (Dec year-end confirmed in FY2025 MD&A); FY2026 H1 core to common 3,598m (+8% reported, +10% CER), core EPS +14% YTD. Not modelled: the Munich Re LTC reinsurance transaction announced with Q2-2026 (capital release would most likely fund extra buybacks, broadly value-neutral at fair price).

bear.rationale: Hong Kong/mainland visitor sales curtailed by regulation or geopolitics, Canada claims weakness persists, a retained-LTC reserve charge and lower rates/markets compress Global WAM fees; buybacks slowed to rebuild LICAT, conversion ~65-70%.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +7.5% (H1 +8% reported/+10% CER; H2-2025 comp includes a strong 3Q25). FY2027-29 7.5-8% aggregate = 10-11% core EPS with ~2.5% buyback shrink, i.e. the low-middle of the 10-12% target; CSM balance growth target 8-10% underwrites it. Fades to 3.5% by year 10.
base.rationale: Conversion 72% near term (below the 75% FY2025 actual to absorb core-vs-net-income leakage and LTC/VA tail), rising to 80% as Asia CSM matures and growth slows (retention needed = g / ROE ~ 3%/17% = 18% at terminal). Cap 14x terminal FCFE = ~11.2x core earnings, a mature-insurer multiple.

bull.rationale: Asia reaches 50%+ of core earnings, core ROE hits 18%+ by 2027 and core EPS compounds at the top of 10-12% plus buybacks; LTC reinsurance releases capital and lifts conversion; Global WAM margins expand with AUMA.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25. Execution is strong (core EPS +14% YTD, CSM +20% YoY, LICAT 136%, financial leverage 22.2% vs 25% target), which argues against a heavier bear weight; but Asia is 47% of core earnings with concentrated China/Hong Kong regulatory exposure and a retained LTC tail, which argues against tilting bull.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
